task.description:
Investigate GH #495 (ISS-0169, MAJOR): LUA-08 through LUA-16 (9 MUST requirements -- LUA-05/06/07 are already RELEASED from prior work today, confirmed via reqctl.py show) need real verification tests against the now-linked, real LuaJIT interpreter (vendored and working per ISS-0161/GH-485). These requirements were never verifiable before -- with stub bindings no script could run, so no limiter/host-function/capability-check could be observed doing anything real. A genuine sandbox bypass (loadfile surviving loadSafeStdlib) was already found and fixed under the sibling issue GH-485 specifically BECAUSE the first thing actually tested against the real interpreter turned out to be broken -- this is the explicit motivating argument in the issue for completing the rest.

Requirements and what needs testing:
- LUA-08: instruction limit actually terminates a runaway loop via lua_sethook
- LUA-09: memory limit actually rejects allocation past the cap
- LUA-10: wall-clock timeout actually interrupts a long script
- LUA-11: variable read/write host functions
- LUA-12: service call host function
- LUA-13: logging host function
- LUA-14: time source host function
- LUA-15: structured failure host function
- LUA-16: runtime error capture

YOUR JOB: read every relevant src/lua/*.zig file (instruction_limiter.zig, memory_limiter.zig, timeout.zig, and each host_api/*.zig file for LUA-11 through LUA-16) to understand the CURRENT state of each -- some limiters already have real-call test coverage added incidentally during GH-500's pin-pattern fix (check src/lua_test_root.zig's most recent test blocks, e.g. 'ISS-0169: the limiter FUNCTION BODIES are analysed' already calls installHook and MemoryLimiter.alloc for REAL -- determine whether this ALREADY satisfies LUA-08/09's acceptance criteria (does the existing test prove ACTUAL TERMINATION, i.e. does calling installHook or exceeding the memory cap actually stop execution, or does it merely prove the functions compile and run without crashing?). Do the same gap analysis for every one of the 9 requirements -- some may be closer to done than the issue implies, others may need substantial new test-writing. Produce a clear per-requirement gap assessment (what exists today, what's missing, what a real passing test for it would need to prove) and route to CODE-DESIGNER with this assessment -- this is real design work (how to structure 9 requirements' worth of tests, whether they share fixtures, whether some genuinely need new production code vs just new tests) -- do not implement directly.
acceptance_criteria: Per-requirement gap assessment produced for all 9 requirements (LUA-08 through LUA-16): current test coverage, what is missing, what a real passing test needs to prove
Determine whether any requirement is ALREADY effectively satisfied by tests added incidentally during GH-500 (do not re-do work that already exists)
Identify which requirements genuinely need new production code vs. only new tests
Routed to CODE-DESIGNER with the full gap assessment, not implemented directly

result.summary:
ISS-0169 tranche 2/3/4 gap assessment (LUA-08 through LUA-16). GH-500's fix made instruction_limiter.zig and memory_limiter.zig COMPILE and added src/lua_test_root.zig test "ISS-0169: the limiter FUNCTION BODIES are analysed" -- this test calls installHook() and MemoryLimiter.alloc() for REAL, but it does NOT satisfy LUA-08/09's acceptance criteria: it only proves the functions execute without crashing (installHook returns without error; a 128-byte alloc succeeds and current_memory_bytes tracks it). It never drives a Lua script through lua_pcall while the limiter is installed, so it proves nothing about actual termination or actual rejection past the cap. Both source files themselves say this explicitly in their own header comments ("This limiter is installed by no code path" / "no code path... LUA-09 has no enforcement. Tranche 2 owns installing it"), and executor.zig's createSandboxedState/executeSource confirm zero call sites for installHook, MemoryLimiter.alloc, or TimeoutContext outside the test root pin. All 9 requirements remain status: IN_PROGRESS in docs/status/requirement_status.yaml, consistent with this finding.

Per-requirement verdicts:

LUA-08 (instruction limit) -- NEEDS PRODUCTION CODE + TEST. installHook() compiles and can be called (GH-500), but createSandboxedState() never calls it -- executeSource creates its Lua state via defaultAlloc with no hook installed. Additionally installHook stores the limiter pointer via a script-writable global (__limiter__ set with lua_setglobal), the same forgery class host_context.zig's REGISTRY_KEY pattern was built to close for capabilities -- a script could nil or overwrite __limiter__. Needed: (1) wire InstructionLimiter into createSandboxedState/executeScript, sourcing max_instructions from somewhere (currently only executeScriptWithManifest's manifest carries max_instructions -- the plain executeScript path has no limit source), (2) move the limiter pointer from the __limiter__ global into LUA_REGISTRYINDEX alongside ExecutionContext, reusing host_context.zig's pattern, (3) a genuinely passing test needs a runaway `while true do end` script executed via lua_pcall through executeScript/executeScriptWithManifest with a low max_instructions, asserting result.success == false and that it terminated (not hung) within a bounded wall-clock budget -- proving actual termination, not merely that installHook can be called.

LUA-09 (memory limit) -- NEEDS PRODUCTION CODE + TEST. MemoryLimiter.alloc() compiles and correctly rejects allocation past max_memory_bytes (verified by reading the function body: `if current + size_delta > max_memory_bytes return null`), but createSandboxedState/createState always uses defaultAlloc (a plain malloc wrapper, unbounded) -- MemoryLimiter.alloc is never passed to lua_newstate. Needed: (1) thread a configurable max_memory_bytes into createSandboxedState and call lua_newstate with MemoryLimiter.alloc + the limiter as `ud`, (2) a genuinely passing test needs a script that allocates past a deliberately tiny cap (e.g. building a large table/string) run through executeScript, asserting result.success == false with a message distinguishable from a generic Lua error -- proving actual allocation rejection surfaces as a script failure, not just that MemoryLimiter.alloc() returns null in isolation.

LUA-10 (wall-clock timeout) -- NEEDS PRODUCTION CODE + TEST, and is architecturally the hardest of the three limiters. TimeoutContext.checkTimeout() compiles and is called once for real by an existing test ("ISS-0153: timeout elapsed-ms no longer uses @divExact"), but that test only proves the struct doesn't panic -- it never runs a script. No code path calls checkTimeout from inside script execution. The design doc (lua-integration.md section 15) is honest that pure host-side timeout-checking cannot interrupt a tight Lua loop or a blocked host call by itself; the practical mechanism (consistent with the codebase's existing LUA_MASKCOUNT hook) is to fold a checkTimeout() call into the SAME instruction-count hook callback LUA-08 installs (check elapsed wall-clock every N instructions, not just instruction count), so LUA-08 and LUA-10 share one hook installation. Needed: (1) extend hookCallback (or create a combined limiter struct) to check TimeoutContext.checkTimeout() in addition to the instruction count and raise on either, (2) decide and document what happens to a script blocked in a host function (call_service) -- LUA-12 is not yet implemented for real so this is currently moot but will need revisiting once call_service does real I/O, (3) a genuinely passing test needs a runaway loop script executed with a short timeout_seconds and NO effective instruction limit (or a very high one), asserting it is interrupted by elapsed time within a bounded margin, not by instruction count -- the two limiters need at least one test each that isolates its own trigger from the other's.

LUA-11 (variable read/write) -- NOT IMPLEMENTED, needs both code and tests. read_variable.zig and write_variable.zig both correctly gate on capability (VARIABLE_READ/VARIABLE_WRITE) and validate argument types (own file headers say so explicitly: "It does NOT implement it: after the gate passes the body still returns nil / stages nothing"). Neither touches any instance state -- read_variable always returns nil regardless of what was "written" and write_variable never stores anything, there is no pending-writes buffer anywhere in executor.zig. Needed: (1) design where instance state lives on ExecutionContext (design section 16.2 sketches a pending_writes staging map applied atomically on script success, discarded on failure -- this does not exist in the current struct, ExecutionContext has no instance_state or pending_writes field), (2) implement the actual get/put against that state from both host functions, (3) implement the atomic-apply-on-success/discard-on-failure semantics in executeSource, (4) tests per design section 16.4 (read, write, write-on-success, write-on-failure/discard, ordering, read-after-write) run through real executeScript calls. This is the largest of the 6 remaining requirements since it requires a new state model, not just wiring an existing one.

LUA-12 (service call) -- PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED, needs code changes + tests. call_service.zig already has substantial real logic: capability gating on the per-service "service:call:<svc_id>" capability (correctly computed before the gate, per design), and when simulation_runtime.get() returns a context it performs a genuine simulated HTTP call via simulation_interceptor.executeMockedServiceCall and returns real (body, status). Outside simulation mode it returns a hardcoded '{}'/200 no-op and never consults service_catalog.zig's ServiceCatalog.lookup -- ServiceCatalog is fully implemented (register/lookup with proper cleanup) but has zero callers anywhere in host_api. The file's own header says explicitly it "does not consult service_catalog.zig... does not return a table" as designed. Needed: (1) decide whether ServiceCatalog needs to become reachable from ExecutionContext (it currently isn't -- there's no service_catalog field on ExecutionContext) and call lookup() to validate svc_id exists / resolve endpoint before any real HTTP path is attempted, (2) either implement a genuine non-simulation HTTP call or explicitly scope that out as future work with the simulation path treated as the only tested path for now, (3) change the return shape from (string, number) to a table per design section 17.1 if that is still the intended contract, (4) tests for: service found + capability granted (simulation path, likely already close to real), service not found, capability denied (already covered by capability_enforcement_test.zig probably), and whichever HTTP-error path exists.

LUA-13 (logging) -- NOT IMPLEMENTED, needs both code and tests. log.zig gates on AUDIT_LOG and validates both arguments are real strings, then does nothing (pushes nil). StructuredLogger.log() is fully implemented and correctly formats a structured entry to stderr via std.debug.print -- but has zero callers; there is no StructuredLogger instance anywhere reachable from ExecutionContext or host_api. Needed: (1) add a StructuredLogger (or a pointer/reference to one) to ExecutionContext, or construct one ad-hoc per call, (2) call it from platformLog with a real StructuredLogEntry built from context.instance_id/actor_id and a trace_id (ExecutionContext currently has no trace_id field either -- design section 18.2 expects one), (3) tests verifying a script's platform.log call produces an entry with the right level/message/correlation IDs -- since the current sink is stderr text, a test likely needs either a swappable writer (test injects a buffer instead of stderr) or to assert against captured stderr, whichever pattern the test guide prefers for this kind of host-side effect.

LUA-14 (time source) -- IMPLEMENTED, NEEDS TESTS ONLY (closest to done of the 9). now.zig calls time_source.TimeSource.now() (or the simulation clock when active) for real and formats a genuine ISO 8601 string; execution_test.zig's sandboxedState()-based tests already exercise adjacent sandbox behavior but no test yet calls platform.now() through an actual script and asserts the returned string is well-formed/parseable, or that os.time/os.date/os.clock are absent from the sandbox (loadSafeStdlib already prunes os per LUA-03 tests, so this may already be incidentally covered -- worth confirming rather than assuming). Needed: tests per design section 19.3 (valid ISO 8601 format, os.time not available, determinism across repeated calls within one script) run through executeScript with a real script body like `return platform.now()`.

LUA-15 (structured failure) -- PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED, needs a moderate code change + tests. fail.zig's platformFail is fully functional today: ungated by design, validates the reason string, stores reason/details/explicit_failure into __failure_reason__/__failure_details__/__explicit_failure__ Lua GLOBALS, then raises. The file's own header names the outstanding defect: these are ordinary script-writable globals (the same forgery class __limiter__ has), a script can nil or overwrite them, and nothing anywhere reads them back -- executor.zig's executeSource never checks __explicit_failure__ after a failed lua_pcall, so a platform.fail call today just looks like any other runtime error to the caller; ScriptResult has no explicit-failure/reason/details fields distinct from error_message. Needed: (1) move the three globals into LUA_REGISTRYINDEX following host_context.zig's pattern (explicitly flagged as tranche-4 follow-up in the file header), (2) read them back in executeSource after a failed pcall and distinguish explicit failure from runtime error in ScriptResult, (3) tests: platform.fail terminates with the given reason, details are carried, and critically a test proving explicit failure is DISTINGUISHABLE from an uncaught runtime error (this doubles as most of LUA-16's "error vs explicit failure" criterion). Emitting a SCRIPT_FAILED event to the event store is engine-layer work per the LUA-07 precedent (design says the executor produces the data, persisting it is the caller's job) -- src/lua/ only needs to produce a structured, readable-back failure result.

LUA-16 (runtime error capture) -- NOT IMPLEMENTED as a distinguishable outcome, needs code + tests, and is coupled to LUA-15. Today an uncaught Lua runtime error (e.g. 1/0, nil-field access) and an explicit platform.fail() both surface identically through executeSource: lua_pcall returns nonzero, the top-of-stack string becomes ScriptResult.error_message, success=false. There is no stack trace capture (design section 21.2's lua_getstack/lua_getinfo walk has no counterpart anywhere in src/lua), no instruction-count-at-failure or capability-snapshot-at-failure recorded, and no way for a caller to tell "the script called platform.fail" apart from "the script crashed". events.zig's ScriptErrorPayload/EventRecord types exist and are correctly structured/memory-managed (deinit frees everything) but have zero construction call sites in src/lua -- they are pure dead types today, same pattern as ServiceCatalog and StructuredLogger. Needed: (1) implement captureStackTrace via lua_getstack/lua_getinfo, (2) after a failed pcall that is NOT an explicit failure (depends on LUA-15's fix landing first or alongside), construct a ScriptErrorPayload with message/stack trace/instruction count (from the LUA-08 limiter, another reason LUA-08 should land before or with LUA-16)/capabilities snapshot, (3) surface this on ScriptResult in some form the caller can consume, (4) tests per design section 21.4: division by zero captured, nil access captured, stack trace has real frame info, instruction count recorded, capability state recorded, and explicit-failure-vs-runtime-error is distinguishable (shared test surface with LUA-15).

Dependency ordering recommendation for CODE-DESIGNER: LUA-08 and LUA-10 share one hook installation and should be designed together. LUA-15 and LUA-16 share the executeSource post-pcall branch and the ScriptResult shape change, and LUA-16's instruction-count field depends on LUA-08's limiter existing. LUA-11, LUA-13 each need one new field added to ExecutionContext (instance-state map; logger/trace_id) and are otherwise independent of the others. LUA-12 is the only one with a real non-trivial existing code path (simulation mode) and needs the smallest proportional change. LUA-14 needs no code changes at all. CLAUDE.md's 4-requirement-per-WF-02-run cap means this cannot be one design/implementation pass; natural batches mirroring the original tranche plan are (LUA-08, LUA-09, LUA-10), (LUA-11, LUA-13), (LUA-12, LUA-15, LUA-16), with LUA-14 folded into whichever batch has room, though CODE-DESIGNER should make the final call once shared fixture/state-model needs (especially for LUA-11) are scoped.
